title: Schema handshake, idempotency, and retry semantics for streamed function-tool calls
creator: Maya Kim
description: Define clear acceptance criteria and operational semantics for a new streaming protocol that supports schema negotiation (handshake), progressive/partial structured output, deterministic tool/function invocation with idempotency tokens, and well-defined retry/error modes. This ticket is a product-facing PRD acceptance checklist that the engineering team will use to implement protocol changes in runtime-1.22 and the Console. It focuses on deterministic behavior for production apps that rely on streaming function/tool calls and structured payloads.
background: Customers building multi-step integrations rely on consistent tool invocation semantics and robust streaming of structured responses. Recent customer incidents and internal experiments showed ambiguity around partial JSON chunks, duplicate tool side-effects on reconnects, and unclear retry policies. This doc captures the acceptance criteria so Eng, DX, and Security agree on a single runtime behavior and testplan.
scope:
- New streaming frame types: handshake/meta, chunk, tool_invoke, tool_result, final, error.
- Schema handshake in the first meta frame of a stream.
- Required invocation metadata: invocation_id (UUID), schema_version, resume_token support.
- Server-side deduplication of tool invocations using invocation_id.
- Deterministic retry/backoff rules and mapping of error codes to retryability.
- Test vectors and dashboards for rollout canary and metrics.
- Backwards-compat mapping layer for legacy 'function_call' field for a transitional period.
out_of_scope:
- Changes to third-party tool-specific APIs (tool backends are out-of-scope except for defining contract).
- UI/Console visualizations beyond basic rollout metrics (separate feature ticket).
- Long-term protocol negotiations beyond schema_version semantics (future RFC if needed).
acceptance_criteria: Handshake: Every new stream must begin with a single meta frame (handshake) that includes: schema_version, schema_hash, required_fields list, optional_fields list, and a boolean 'supports_resume'. The handshake frame must be the first byte of the stream and be parseable independently.

Progressive payloads: The model may emit structured output across multiple chunk frames. Each chunk frame must include a 'chunk_index' and 'byte_range' and be valid UTF-8. Concatenating chunk payloads in chunk_index order must yield a JSON payload that validates against the provided schema_version. Clients can also parse incremental NDJSON records if the schema indicates 'record_streaming'.

Finalization: The stream must include a final frame with 'final': true and 'final_schema_hash'. The final frame indicates the server can perform schema validation and mark the stream complete. Missing final frame within stream_timeout must result in an error frame with code ERR_STREAM_TRUNCATED.

Tool invocation format: To request a tool, the stream must include a tool_invoke frame that contains tool_id, invocation_id (UUID v4), params (JSON string or chunk reference), and idempotency_hint. The params payload must conform to the tool's registered JSON schema; mismatches produce ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH and no backend call is made.

Idempotent execution: The runtime must pass invocation_id to tool backends and deduplicate calls with the same invocation_id for the lifetime of the configured dedupe window (default 24h). Duplicate invocations with identical invocation_id must return cached tool_result frames instead of re-executing side effects.

Retry policy: Only calls to tools marked 'idempotent' in the tool registry may be auto-retried by the runtime. Retryable errors include ERR_TRANSIENT_NETWORK and ERR_TOOL_BUSY. Auto-retry attempts <= 2 with exponential backoff starting at 200ms. Non-idempotent tools are not auto-retried; runtime must emit a recoverable=false error frame and surface the event in the Console.

Error frames: All error frames must include error_code (from defined set), human_message, recoverable (true|false), and optional diagnostic_id. Mandatory error codes: ERR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, ERR_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, ERR_INVOCATION_FAILED, ERR_PARSE_ERROR, ERR_STREAM_TRUNCATED. Mapping to retry behavior must be documented in code and tests.

Resume semantics: If a client disconnects and reconnects within the handshake-supported resume window, it may present the last resume_token from the previous stream. The runtime must allow resumption only when the server-side buffer and tool invocation are still available; otherwise emit ERR_RESUME_NOT_AVAILABLE. Resume behavior must never re-trigger side-effects for completed invocations (use invocation_id to dedupe).

Deterministic ordering: For streams containing multiple tool_invokes, tool_invokes must be executed in the order received unless the stream requests parallel_execution=true. Console telemetry must reflect actual execution order and outcomes.

Instrumentation: Each stream and tool invocation must log telemetry labels: schema_version, tool_id, invocation_id, outcome (success|failure|timeout), latency_ms, and retry_count. These metrics must be visible in a rollout dashboard and used for canary gating.

Test vectors: Implementation must pass an automated suite of at least 12 test vectors including: partial-chunk assembly, handshake absent, mismatched final_schema, duplicate invocation_id, network reconnect with resume, tool timeout leading to non-retryable error, and parallel_invokes concurrency. Tests must be checked into runtime/integration-tests and run on PRs targeting runtime-1.22.

Backward compatibility: The runtime must accept legacy 'function_call' shaped frames for 6 months and map them to the new tool_invoke format. Logs must include a warning when legacy frames are received.

API docs: Public API and SDK changelog must include sample code for streaming with handshake, how to generate and persist invocation_id, and guidance on idempotency for tool authors. Docs must be published before the runtime rollout reaches 50%.

Security: Any tool invocation that triggers external network calls must be flagged for review by Security before release. Secrets or credentials must never be emitted in cleartext in chunk frames; runtime must redact any field annotated as 'sensitive' in the registered tool schema.

Rollout guardrails: Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic for 1 week, 25% for 2 weeks, 100% after metrics pass. Canary passing criteria: error_rate change <= +0.5% absolute, p95 latency increase <= 10%, and no customer-impacting ERR_INVOCATION_FAILED incidents in canary tenants.
Operator controls: Console must expose a kill-switch to disable auto-retry globally and a per-tool toggle for idempotent enforcement within the release window.
success_metrics: <1% user-visible errors caused by streaming schema issues in first 30 days post-rollout
0 production incidents caused by duplicate side-effects from tool invocations within 90 days
Telemetry coverage >= 99% for invocation_id and outcome labels
All integration tests green in CI and no regressions in runtime-1.22 benchmark suite
risks: Tool backends must adopt invocation_id dedupe or we risk duplicate side-effects; coordination risk with third-party tool owners.
Resume semantics add server state and storage costs for resume windows; needs SRE checks for scalability.
Mis-implemented schema handshake could cause older clients to break; requires robust backwards compatibility testing.
Exposing too many auto-retry behaviors could mask downstream failures and increase cost if retries executed against expensive backends.
